stories.headline: Fixing the taka means fixing the budget, banks and exports, columnists argue
stories.summary: Columnists Dr Mohammad Abdul Hannan Pradhan and Murad Mia argue the taka's fall was not an accident: the government covered budget deficits by borrowing from the central bank, creating money, while Bangladesh Bank sold dollars to defend the rate, so reserves fell from nearly $48 billion in August 2021 to $20-25 billion by mid-2024 and the taka slid from about 85 to over 122 per US dollar.
stories.why_it_matters: The taka's slide, the $48 billion to $20-25 billion reserve fall and the 85-to-122 exchange rate are the core numbers for any BCS/Bank written answer on the exchange rate, and the column gives the comparative cases — Brazil 1994, Korea 1997, India 1991, Sri Lanka 2022 — that make such an answer.
stories.exam_facts: The columnists write that headline inflation ran around 8 to 9% through 2025-2026, driven by imported fuel, fertiliser and food; they argue a weak taka is no gift to exporters because garments depend on imported cotton, yarn and machinery; they credit Bangladesh with largely stopping direct deficit financing, raising the policy rate to 9.50%, moving from a rigid peg toward market-based reference rates and rebuilding reserves to around $31-32 billion by late 2026; their six prescriptions are a legal limit on central bank deficit financing, an honest floating exchange rate with published intervention data, bank repair including limits on unhedged dollar borrowing, formal remittance channels, stronger RMG backward linkage and diversified exports, and deeper taka bond markets.
stories.exam_relevance: Exchange rate, reserves, inflation, central bank financing of deficits, comparative currency crises — core BCS/Bank economy topics.
stories.key_people: Dr Mohammad Abdul Hannan Pradhan, SUST economics professor; Murad Mia, SUST economics undergraduate
stories.figures: Reserves nearly $48 billion (Aug 2021) to $20-25 billion (mid-2024); taka about 85 to over 122 per US dollar; inflation 8-9% in 2025-2026; policy rate 9.50%; reserves recovered to around $31-32 billion by late 2026.

stories.headline: PM pledges trillion-dollar climate-resilient economy and five-point climate agenda at COP31
stories.summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman told the High-Level Segment of COP31 in Antalya on 12 November that Bangladesh will build a trillion-dollar, climate-resilient and sustainable economy, guided by 'Bangladesh Before All', although the country contributes less than 0.5% of global greenhouse gas emissions. He set a 2030 target of 20% of electricity from renewables, pledged 250 million trees in five years and called for grants, not loans, for climate-vulnerable countries.
stories.why_it_matters: The trillion-dollar pledge, the 20% renewables target, the 250 million trees and the five-point agenda are the quotable core of Bangladesh's COP31 position — the exact material BCS/Bank questions on climate diplomacy ask for.
stories.exam_facts: The government is developing 4,000 megawatts of solar power with special tax incentives and promoting waste-to-energy projects, electric vehicles, jute bags and a national carbon-trading framework, with nearly 300 LEED-certified garment factories already operating; the prime minister also announced excavating 20,000 kilometres of rivers and canals, the Padma Barrage and Teesta Barrage Master Plan and mangrove restoration on reclaimed coastal land; his five urgent actions are at least 50% of climate finance to adaptation, debt relief including Debt-for-Climate Swaps and Climate-Resilient Debt Clauses, fair access to climate-friendly technologies, a fair energy transition through affordable finance and skills, and adopting the Belem-Antalya Action Mechanism for a just transition; he thanked Turkiye for hosting and Australia for leading the negotiations.
stories.exam_relevance: COP31, climate finance, adaptation, renewable energy, LDC climate diplomacy — core BCS/Bank environment and foreign-policy topics.
stories.figures: Less than 0.5% of global emissions; 20% renewables by 2030; 4,000 MW solar; nearly 300 LEED-certified RMG factories; 250 million trees in 5 years; 20,000 km of rivers and canals; at least 50% of climate finance to adaptation.

stories.headline: Nvidia chief Jensen Huang resigns amid scandal; shares down about 25% from peak
stories.summary: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang, 63, resigned on 12 November after revelations of two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman accused of spying for China, ending his 33-year run at the helm of the company he co-founded in 1993. Chief financial officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO, the stock was already down about 25% from its early-October all-time high, and shareholders have filed a class action lawsuit.
stories.why_it_matters: The fall of the AI boom's most prominent chief executive, the governance failure behind it and the 25% share slide are the kind of global business event BCS/Bank current-affairs and corporate-governance questions use.
stories.exam_facts: Huang also gave up his board seat, and the board appointed Harvey Jones, a former chief executive of chip design software firm Synopsys, as its first-ever chair; US intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this spring alleging Alice Huang was an asset of China's Ministry of State Security, and Beijing has rejected the spying allegations; the board announced a probe on Sunday into reporting that Huang had been the target of a 'foreign intelligence effort'; the New York Times reported a second affair with Kimberly Powell, 48, Nvidia's vice president of health care, citing video evidence; Huang had been married to Lori Huang for more than 40 years and had repeatedly avoided naming a successor; Kress joined Nvidia as finance chief in 2013 after nearly 25 years in finance roles at Cisco and Microsoft.
stories.exam_relevance: Artificial intelligence industry, corporate governance, leadership succession, US-China technology tensions — BCS/Bank international current-affairs topics.
stories.key_people: Jensen Huang, Nvidia co-founder and former CEO; Colette Kress, interim CEO; Harvey Jones, board chair; Kimberly Powell, Nvidia vice president of health care
stories.figures: Huang 63 years old; 33-year run at the helm; Nvidia founded 1993; stock down about 25% from early-October all-time high; Kress finance chief since 2013.

stories.headline: Bangladesh Bank sells $205m to banks; dollar rate falls below Tk125
stories.summary: Bangladesh Bank sold $205 million from its foreign exchange reserves to commercial banks through an auction on 12 November at Tk124.74 per dollar, and remittance houses lowered their dollar selling rates to below Tk125 from Tk125.30-Tk125.40 earlier in the day. After the sale the reserve position stood at $29.82 billion, down from $30.12 billion the previous day.
stories.why_it_matters: A $205 million intervention, the Tk124.74 auction rate and the $29.82 billion reserve level are the live numbers for BCS/Bank questions on the exchange rate and reserve management — and they connect directly to the taka op-ed in CA01.
stories.exam_facts: Earlier in November the central bank sold $120 million at Tk124.30-Tk124.35 per dollar; the central bank instructed participating banks not to resell the purchased dollars in the interbank market, warning it could disrupt the foreign exchange market; banks bought more than $300 million from remittance houses on the day, partly because rising fuel prices had increased import costs; a senior banker said the auction notice went out at 1:20pm and that a morning announcement could have pushed the rate lower, since demand for foreign currency is generally higher at the beginning of the month; central bank spokesperson Arief Hossain Khan confirmed the sale.
stories.exam_relevance: Foreign exchange reserves, central bank intervention, dollar-taka rate, remittance — core BCS/Bank economy and banking topics.
stories.key_people: Arief Hossain Khan, Bangladesh Bank spokesperson
stories.figures: $205 million sold at Tk124.74; rates below Tk125 from Tk125.30-Tk125.40; reserves $29.82 billion from $30.12 billion; $120 million sold earlier in November at Tk124.30-Tk124.35; banks bought over $300 million from remittance houses.

stories.headline: Dhaka-Ankara ties enter a new phase as Tarique and Erdogan meet for the second time
stories.summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan held their second meeting in two months in Antalya on 10 November 2026, after a first meeting in New York on 22 September, with talks centred on trade, investment, energy, mineral resources, aviation and the defence industry. The prime minister's wife Zubaida Rahman also met Turkish First Lady Emine Erdogan, and analysts say the meetings signal a move to a more institutionalised and strategic relationship.
stories.why_it_matters: Two leader-level meetings in under two months, the Two-Plus-Two dialogue plan and the defence-industry track are the concrete facts for BCS/Bank questions on Bangladesh-Turkiye relations and foreign policy.
stories.exam_facts: The two sides discussed deepening and diversifying defence cooperation, joint investment and developing a defence industry in Bangladesh with Turkish investment, plus climate risks and a lasting solution to the Rohingya crisis; in June 2026 Turkish foreign minister Hakan Fidan visited Dhaka and the two countries announced plans for a joint ministerial committee on defence and foreign affairs, annual foreign-minister meetings and regular Two-Plus-Two meetings; Army Chief General Waker-Uz-Zaman visited Turkiye in July 2026; Turkish trade minister Omer Bolat visited Bangladesh in January 2025 and deputy foreign minister Berris Ekinci attended the fourth round of political consultations in October 2025 and the new government's swearing-in in February 2026; the analysis notes Turkiye withdrew its ambassador in 2016 after death sentences for Jamaat-e-Islami leaders, Bangladesh's letter of support after the failed July 2016 coup and Emine Erdogan's September 2017 visit after the Rohingya influx as turning points, and cites Arcelik's acquisition of a majority stake in Singer Bangladesh as a sign of Turkish business interest.
stories.exam_relevance: Bangladesh-Turkiye relations, defence cooperation, foreign policy, Rohingya diplomacy — core BCS/Bank international-relations topics.
stories.key_people: Tarique Rahman, Prime Minister; Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Turkish President; Zubaida Rahman; Emine Erdogan, Turkish First Lady; Hakan Fidan, Turkish Foreign Minister; Khalilur Rahman, Foreign Minister
stories.figures: First meeting 22 September 2026 in New York; second meeting 10 November 2026 in Antalya; ambassador withdrawn 2016; failed coup July 2016; Emine Erdogan visit September 2017.

stories.headline: US ambassador meets Indian High Commissioner in Dhaka amid Hasina extradition row
stories.summary: US Ambassador to Bangladesh Brent T. Christensen met Indian High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi in Dhaka on the morning of 12 November 2026. A source at the US Embassy confirmed the meeting but said it was not known what the two diplomats discussed; Christensen arrived in Dhaka on 12 January 2026 and Trivedi arrived in June 2026.
stories.why_it_matters: A meeting between the US and Indian envoys in Dhaka, days after the government challenged Hasina to seek extradition, is the kind of diplomatic signal BCS/Bank questions on India-Bangladesh relations and the Hasina case ask about.
stories.exam_facts: The meeting comes against a charged political atmosphere as Dhaka seeks the extradition of deposed former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, who has been living in India since 5 August 2024, while Hasina herself has pledged to return to Bangladesh in December 2026.
stories.exam_relevance: Diplomacy, India-Bangladesh relations, extradition — core BCS/Bank foreign-policy topics.
stories.key_people: Brent T. Christensen, US Ambassador to Bangladesh; Dinesh Trivedi, Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh
stories.figures: Meeting on 12 November 2026; Christensen arrived 12 January 2026; Trivedi arrived June 2026; Hasina in India since 5 August 2024.

stories.headline: HSC supplementary exams from 1 December; schedule published
stories.summary: The Inter-Education Board Examination Controllers Committee published the schedule for the 2026 HSC and equivalent supplementary examinations on 12 November 2026. The examinations begin on 1 December with English First Paper and continue until 15 December, when the written papers end with Economics and Arabic and the practical examinations must also be completed.
stories.why_it_matters: The HSC supplementary schedule — 1 to 15 December, English first, Economics and Arabic last — is a direct education-desk fact for candidates, and the supplementary route itself is a live admissions question.
stories.exam_facts: Bangla First and Second Papers will be held on 2 December; Physics, Accounting and Logic on 3 December; Information and Communication Technology on 5 December; the committee published the schedule on Thursday, 12 November 2026.
stories.exam_relevance: Education boards, HSC examinations, supplementary examinations — BCS/Bank education topics.
stories.figures: Examinations 1-15 December 2026; English First Paper 1 December; Bangla papers 2 December; Physics, Accounting, Logic 3 December; ICT 5 December; written ends 15 December.

stories.headline: Bangladesh Bank revamps Tk1,500 crore refinance scheme for farmers and small entrepreneurs
stories.summary: Bangladesh Bank's Financial Inclusion Department issued revamped guidelines on 12 November 2026 for its Tk1,500 crore revolving refinance scheme for marginal farmers, low-income professionals, small entrepreneurs, students and remittance-recipient families, replacing all previous circulars including FID Circular-01/2021. Banks get refinancing at 1% a year and may lend at most 7% a year, with at least 25% of the loans going to female entrepreneurs.
stories.why_it_matters: A Tk1,500 crore scheme at 1% refinance and 7% to borrowers, with a 25% women's share and Tk10 lakh individual cap, is exactly the kind of financial-inclusion policy BCS/Bank banking questions test.
stories.exam_facts: The scheme runs for five years on Bangladesh Bank's own funds; marginal and landless farmers holding Farmer Smart Cards under the Department of Agricultural Extension get priority loans up to Tk10 lakh; individual loans go up to Tk10 lakh and group loans up to Tk8 lakh per member, for groups of two to five people, with a maximum of Tk40 lakh per group; no security collateral can be demanded for loans up to Tk5 lakh, though personal guarantees may be required; loans carry a maximum grace period of 6 months and a total repayment tenor of up to 5 years, with interest calculated quarterly on a diminishing balance; under student banking, loans come with parental repayment guarantees for university, college and madrasa (Alim/Fazil) students, while school students can borrow for educational materials; corrected 13 Nov 2026: TBS, Daily Inqilab and tob.news all report 1% refinance, 7% borrower max and a Tk40 lakh group cap.
stories.exam_relevance: Financial inclusion, refinance schemes, SME and agricultural credit, women's entrepreneurship — core BCS/Bank banking topics.
stories.key_people: Bangladesh Bank, Financial Inclusion Department; Department of Agricultural Extension
stories.figures: Tk1,500 crore revolving scheme; 5-year tenure; refinance to banks 1% a year; borrowers max 7% a year; at least 25% to female entrepreneurs; individual loans up to Tk10 lakh; group cap Tk40 lakh; no collateral up to Tk5 lakh; grace period up to 6 months; tenor up to 5 years.

stories.headline: Bhola Cyclone of 1970 remembered: deadliest tropical cyclone on record
stories.summary: Survivors recalled the devastation of the Bhola Cyclone of 12 November 1970, the deadliest tropical cyclone on record, as calls grow for 12 November to be observed as Coast Day. In a single night more than a million people lost their lives along the coast, which was submerged under 17 to 18 feet of water, after timely weather warnings, cyclone shelters and strong embankments were all lacking.
stories.why_it_matters: The 1970 Bhola Cyclone — the deadliest on record, over a million dead in one night — is a standard BCS/Bank history and disaster-management fact, and the Coast Day call keeps it current.
stories.exam_facts: The article tells the story of Mofiza Begum, 35, of Char Jatin on Manpura Island in Bhola, who lost her daughter and was swept nearly 100 kilometres to the mouth of the Karnaphuli River in Chittagong, surviving on the carcass of a dead cow and waving a piece of colourful polythene on a stick until a steamer rescued her; according to records from the World Meteorological Organization, the cyclone remains the deadliest tropical cyclone in recorded history; elderly residents of Bhola, Patuakhali and Lakshmipur recall water rising with startling speed, driven by winds from the southeast, with people taking refuge first on the plinths of their homes, then on elevated platforms, then by climbing trees.
stories.exam_relevance: Disaster history, cyclone management, coastal Bangladesh, 1970 — core BCS/Bank history and geography topics.
stories.key_people: Mofiza Begum, cyclone survivor; Rafiqul Islam Montu, author
stories.figures: 12 November 1970; more than 1 million dead in one night; coast under 17-18 feet of water; Mofiza swept nearly 100 km; WMO records it as the deadliest tropical cyclone on record.

stories.headline: Bangladesh Bank sets strict qualifications for CFO, CITO and company secretary posts at NBFIs
stories.summary: Bangladesh Bank has set strict eligibility criteria for appointments to three senior posts — chief financial officer, chief information technology officer (CITO) and company secretary — at non-bank financial institutions (NBFIs), in a directive issued on 12 November 2026. Candidates convicted of criminal offences, regulatory violations, corruption or moral turpitude are barred, as are loan defaulters and bankrupts, and no prior approval from Bangladesh Bank is required for the appointments.
stories.why_it_matters: The 10-year and 8-year experience rules, the Tk1,000 crore threshold and the fit-and-proper bars are the testable facts of a new banking-governance rule — and the post is CITO — Bangladesh Bank’s own term since its 2018 circular — and the rule covers NBFIs only.
stories.exam_facts: For CFOs at institutions with loans outstanding above Tk1,000 crore, candidates need at least 10 years' experience including 3 years in accounting and taxation; below Tk1,000 crore the minimum is 8 years including 3 years in accounting and tax work; CFO candidates need a master's in finance, accounting or bank management (MBM) or a postgraduate degree in finance, accounting or banking, with CA, CMA or CFA preferred; a CITO needs at least 8 years in IT including 5 years in banks or financial institutions, with a bachelor's in IT, computer science, physics, applied physics, mathematics, statistics or EEE; a company secretary needs 8 years in a bank or financial institution including 4 years in board secretariat or compliance, or 3 years as a company secretary at a listed company, plus a Chartered Secretary qualification recognised by the Institute of Chartered Secretaries of Bangladesh and at least a bachelor's degree; corrected 13 Nov 2026: TBS confirms the directive covers NBFIs only, calls the post CITO, and adds a 31 December 2029 deadline for existing officials, a three-month cap on acting appointments and a full-time-only rule. Existing officials who do not fully meet the criteria have until 31 December 2029 to do so; the posts must be filled full-time (no contractual or part-time appointments), and an acting appointment may last at most three months.
stories.exam_relevance: Banking governance, fit-and-proper criteria, NBFI regulation, professional qualifications — core BCS/Bank banking topics.
stories.key_people: Bangladesh Bank; Institute of Chartered Secretaries of Bangladesh
stories.figures: CFO: 10 years above Tk1,000 crore, 8 years below, both including 3 years in accounting/tax; CITO: 8 years in IT including 5 in banks/FIs; company secretary: 8 years including 4 in board secretariat/compliance, or 3 years as company secretary at a listed company.

stories.headline: Bangladesh-India consular dialogue scheduled for November will not take place
stories.summary: The fifth round of the Bangladesh-India consular dialogue, which was being prepared for November in Dhaka, has not gone ahead, despite an inter-ministerial meeting on 3 November to prepare for the talks. Officials say the two countries' bilateral mechanisms appear to have stalled, with little tangible progress on key areas of cooperation, although Bangladesh and India have over 40 bilateral mechanisms covering water, trade, border management and consular issues.
stories.why_it_matters: A stalled fifth round of consular dialogue, after a preparatory meeting on 3 November, is the concrete evidence for BCS/Bank questions on the current state of Bangladesh-India relations.
stories.exam_facts: The consular dialogue mechanism was instituted in 2017 to strengthen people-to-people contacts through a regular channel on consular, visa and mutual legal assistance matters; the fourth round was held on 29 May 2024 in New Delhi, where the two sides discussed consular issues, visa matters, repatriation, mutual legal assistance and extradition cases and agreed to strengthen the bilateral Revised Travel Arrangement; the November round was supposed to discuss cross-border issues, border management, streamlining visa processes, repatriating citizens detained in either country, and securing the release and repatriation of fishermen.
stories.exam_relevance: Bangladesh-India relations, consular affairs, visas, repatriation, bilateral mechanisms — core BCS/Bank foreign-policy topics.
stories.figures: Fifth round planned for November 2026, not taking place; inter-ministerial meeting 3 November 2026; over 40 bilateral mechanisms; mechanism instituted 2017; fourth round 29 May 2024 in New Delhi.

stories.headline: Parliamentary body seeks action plans to cut losses and revive closed state factories
stories.summary: The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Public Undertakings recommended action plans on 12 November 2026 to reduce losses in state-owned industrial enterprises, revive closed factories and make proper use of unused government land and assets. At its 9th meeting, chaired by Chief Whip Nurul Islam Moni, the committee reviewed the finances of enterprises under BSEC, BSFIC and BSCIC and their prospects for reopening closed factories.
stories.why_it_matters: State-owned enterprise losses, closed sugar mills and unused government land are standard BCS/Bank public-finance and industrial-policy material, and the 9th meeting's recommendations are the current facts.
stories.exam_facts: The committee recommended identifying the reasons behind the losses of different BSEC enterprises and preparing effective, institution-specific action plans; it stressed resolving ownership disputes and legal complications involving long-closed industrial units, making proper use of their unused land and assets, and assessing the feasibility of reopening the factories; discussing BSFIC's closed sugar mills, the committee considered the prospects for restarting them, increasing sugarcane production and encouraging farmers to cultivate more sugarcane.
stories.exam_relevance: State-owned enterprises, public undertakings, industrial policy, parliamentary oversight — core BCS/Bank economy topics.
stories.key_people: Nurul Islam Moni, Chief Whip and chairman of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Public Undertakings
stories.figures: 9th meeting of the committee, 12 November 2026; three corporations reviewed: BSEC, BSFIC, BSCIC.

stories.headline: Health sector spent under 2% of its development budget in the first quarter, columnist writes
stories.summary: Columnist Dr Rumana Huque writes that Bangladesh's health sector faces a troubling paradox: public hospitals struggle with shortages of medicines, diagnostic equipment and professionals, while in the first quarter of 2026-27 (July-September) the Health Services Division spent only 1.78% of its direct ADP allocation and the Medical Education and Family Welfare Division only 1.86%, together just Tk209 crore of Tk11,513 crore, against a national ADP implementation rate of 3.89%.
stories.why_it_matters: The 1.78% and 1.86% spending rates, the Tk209 crore of Tk11,513 crore and the Tk23,577 crore unused block allocation are the hard numbers for any BCS/Bank answer on health budgeting and ADP implementation.
stories.exam_facts: Huque argues the explanation lies in the discontinuation of the Sector-Wide Approach: the fourth Health, Population and Nutrition Sector Programme ended in June 2024 and the proposed fifth programme was discontinued during the interim government, while the ministry abolished the line director and programme manager posts in September 2025, so development work must now go through individual Development Project Proposals that need technical design, costing, feasibility assessment and multiple approvals; she writes that Tk23,577 crore in block allocations for the two divisions was reportedly unused in the quarter, that a block allocation is a provision for prospective projects and cannot be spent without approved DPPs and appointed project personnel, and that her prescriptions are a dedicated multidisciplinary project preparation team, a prioritised costed project pipeline, quarterly monitoring and better coordination of development and operating budgets.
stories.exam_relevance: Health budget, ADP implementation, development project proposals, public financial management — core BCS/Bank economy and governance topics.
stories.key_people: Dr Rumana Huque, Dhaka University economics professor and ARK Foundation executive director
stories.figures: HSD 1.78% and MEFWD 1.86% of direct ADP allocation in Q1 FY2026-27; Tk209 crore spent of Tk11,513 crore; Tk23,577 crore block allocations unused; national ADP rate 3.89%; fourth HPNSP ended June 2024; posts abolished September 2025.

phrases.Bangla meaning: আর্থিক অন্তর্ভুক্তি; সুবিধাবঞ্চিতদের আনুষ্ঠানিক ব্যাংকিংয়ে আনা
phrases.English explanation: Making formal financial services — bank accounts, credit, insurance — available and affordable to people and groups who are usually excluded from them.
phrases.Original example 1: Bangladesh Bank has issued a comprehensive, unified policy revamping its Tk 1,500 crore scheme aimed at bolstering financial inclusion for marginal farmers, low-income professionals, small business owners, students, and remittance-recipient families.
phrases.Original example 2: The central bank expects that this streamlined framework will significantly expand credit flow to underserved communities, strengthen financial inclusion, and support the country's socioeconomic development by driving grassroots economic growth and employment generation.

phrases.Article headline: Bangladesh Bank issues revamped Tk 1,500cr refinance scheme for financial inclusion

phrases.English explanation: Serious dishonesty or depraved conduct that shows a person is unfit for a position of trust.

phrases.English explanation: Money provided by developed countries and international funds to help developing countries cut emissions and adapt to climate change.

phrases.Article headline: Bangladesh Bank sells $205m to banks, dollar rate falls below Tk125
phrases.Exam value: Bangladesh-specific banking term — remittance houses are central to the dollar market.

phrases.English explanation: Standing frameworks or channels through which two countries regularly discuss and manage an issue.

mcqs.question: In the dollar-sale story, what is a 'remittance'?

options.A: A loan from Bangladesh Bank to a commercial bank
options.B: Money sent home by workers abroad
options.C: A tax collected on imported goods at the port
options.D: The fee a bank charges for exchanging currency

mcqs.explanation: A remittance is money sent home by a person working abroad; remittance houses trade the dollars that flow in. (CA04)

mcqs.question: What does 'budget deficit' mean?

options.A: Spending more than income
options.B: A surplus kept in the central bank's reserves
options.C: The total value of exports in a financial year
options.D: A loan taken from the International Monetary Fund

mcqs.explanation: A deficit is the amount by which spending exceeds income. The columnists argue the government covered its budget deficit by borrowing from the central bank. (CA01)

mcqs.question: What is 'hyperinflation'?

options.A: A small, controlled annual rise in the general price level
options.B: A fall in the general price level
options.C: Stable prices over a long period

mcqs.explanation: Hyperinflation is extremely rapid and out-of-control inflation. Brazil suffered decades of hyperinflation, the columnists write. (CA01)

mcqs.question: What does it mean for a country to 'devalue' its currency?

options.A: To let its value rise freely in the market
options.B: To fix its value permanently to gold
options.C: To officially reduce its value
options.D: To ban its use in foreign trade

mcqs.explanation: To devalue is to officially reduce a currency's value. India devalued in steps during its 1991 crisis, the columnists write. (CA01)

mcqs.question: 'Unhedged dollar borrowing' means borrowing in dollars...

options.A: Without protection against exchange-rate moves
options.B: With a full government guarantee covering every possible loss
options.C: Only from the central bank at a fixed rate
options.D: For a period of less than one month

mcqs.explanation: Unhedged means unprotected against risk. The columnists urge strict limits on unhedged dollar borrowing by companies. (CA01)

mcqs.question: What is a 'rigid peg' in exchange-rate policy?

options.A: A rate that changes every hour with the market
options.B: A rate fixed against another currency
options.C: A tax on foreign currency transactions
options.D: A limit on how much foreign currency a bank may hold

mcqs.explanation: A peg is an exchange rate fixed at a set level. Bangladesh moved from a rigid peg toward market-based reference rates, the columnists write. (CA01)

mcqs.question: To 'restructure' a debt means to...

options.A: Repay it in full immediately
options.B: Cancel it without any conditions
options.C: Refuse to recognise it as a liability

mcqs.explanation: To restructure a debt is to change its repayment terms. Sri Lanka restructured its debt under its IMF programme, the columnists write. (CA01)

mcqs.question: What are a country's 'foreign exchange reserves'?

options.A: The total tax collected in a year
options.B: The value of all goods exported in a year
options.C: A central bank's stock of foreign currency
options.D: The money printed by the central bank each month

mcqs.explanation: Reserves are the central bank's stock of foreign currency. Gross reserves fell from nearly $48 billion in August 2021 to $20-25 billion by mid-2024. (CA01)

mcqs.question: In the dollar-sale story, what is an 'auction'?

options.A: A sale to the highest bidder
options.B: A fixed-price sale set by the central bank
options.C: A secret agreement between two banks
options.D: A government ban on selling dollars

mcqs.explanation: An auction sells to the highest bidder. Bangladesh Bank sold $205 million to banks through an auction at Tk124.74 per dollar. (CA04)

mcqs.question: What does 'refinancing' mean in the Tk1,500 crore scheme?

options.A: Banks writing off their bad loans entirely
options.B: Bangladesh Bank lending to banks so they can lend onward
options.C: Borrowers repaying their old loans early to avoid paying further interest

mcqs.explanation: Under the scheme, participating banks secure refinancing from Bangladesh Bank at 1% a year and lend onward at most 7%. (CA08)

mcqs.question: What does 'financial inclusion' mean?

options.A: Requiring every bank to publish its annual profits in newspapers
options.B: Closing small bank branches in villages
options.C: Bringing underserved people into formal banking
options.D: Raising interest rates to attract deposits

mcqs.explanation: Financial inclusion means bringing excluded people into formal banking. The Tk1,500 crore scheme aims to bolster it for marginal farmers and small entrepreneurs. (CA08)

mcqs.question: What does 'moral turpitude' mean?

options.A: A minor administrative error
options.B: A delay in filing tax returns with the revenue authority
options.C: A disagreement over office policy

mcqs.explanation: Moral turpitude is serious dishonesty or depraved conduct. People convicted of it are barred from the CFO, CITO and company secretary posts. (CA10)

mcqs.question: According to the columnists, what caused the taka's fall?

options.A: A strong US dollar and speculation by foreign currency traders
options.B: Deficit financing and dollar sales to defend the rate
options.C: Falling remittances and export orders

mcqs.explanation: The columnists argue the government covered deficits by borrowing from the central bank, creating money, while Bangladesh Bank sold dollars to defend the rate, so reserves fell from nearly $48 billion to $20-25 billion. (CA01)

mcqs.question: What share of climate finance did the prime minister urge be allocated to adaptation?

options.A: At least 50%
options.B: At least 25% of the total
options.C: At least 75%

mcqs.explanation: At COP31 the prime minister urged that at least 50% of international climate finance be allocated to adaptation. (CA02)

mcqs.question: Who became Nvidia's interim CEO after Jensen Huang resigned?

options.A: Harvey Jones
options.B: Kimberly Powell
options.C: Colette Kress

mcqs.explanation: Chief financial officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor. (CA03)

mcqs.question: At what rate did Bangladesh Bank sell $205 million on 12 November?

options.A: Tk124.30 per dollar
options.B: Tk125.30 per dollar, the morning rate
options.C: Tk124.90 per dollar

mcqs.explanation: Bangladesh Bank sold the dollars at Tk124.74 each through the auction on 12 November. (CA04)

mcqs.question: When did Tarique Rahman and Erdogan hold their second meeting?

options.A: 10 November 2026 in Antalya
options.B: 22 September 2026 in New York
options.C: 12 November 2026 in Dhaka

mcqs.explanation: The second meeting took place on 10 November 2026 in Antalya; the first was on 22 September 2026 in New York. (CA05)

mcqs.question: What did the US Embassy say about the Christensen-Trivedi meeting?

options.A: The two envoys signed a new bilateral trade and investment agreement
options.B: It confirmed the meeting but not what was discussed
options.C: The meeting was about the extradition treaty
options.D: No meeting took place at all

mcqs.explanation: A source at the US Embassy confirmed the meeting to UNB but said it was not known what the two diplomats discussed. (CA06)

mcqs.question: When do the 2026 HSC supplementary examinations begin?

options.A: 15 December 2026, with Economics and Arabic
options.B: 2 December 2026
options.C: 1 December 2026

mcqs.explanation: The examinations begin on 1 December 2026 with English First Paper and continue until 15 December. (CA07)

mcqs.question: Under the refinance scheme, what is the maximum interest banks may charge borrowers?

options.A: 0.5% per annum
options.B: 1% per annum
options.C: 7% per annum

mcqs.explanation: Banks get refinancing at 1% and may charge borrowers at most 7% a year — TBS, Daily Inqilab and tob.news all report the same figures; UNB’s 0.5%/5% were wrong. (CA08)

mcqs.question: What does the World Meteorological Organization record say about the 1970 Bhola Cyclone?

options.A: The deadliest tropical cyclone on record
